source.title: Learning Rates as a Function of Batch Size: A Random Matrix Theory Approach to Neural Network Training
source.authors: Diego Granziol; Stefan Zohren; Stephen J. Roberts

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or corruption that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training accuracy and training-error outcomes while testing batch-size learning-rate scaling; these results bear on V1, but it does not test the full set of V1 conditions.
record.gate_note: Training-error curves and stated training accuracies bear on V1. The paper's Hessian-spectrum measurements and validation/test metrics do not measure the claim's training-error outcome. It does not test the other versions' stated mechanisms.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own SGD training classification outcomes for VGG-16 on CIFAR-100, using the method and measure named in V1. It varies batch size and learning rate rather than label corruption.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that, up to a threshold, SGD learning rates should scale linearly with batch size and Adam learning rates with its square root. They also conclude that curvature-based learning-rate and momentum estimation should use the batch Hessian rather than the empirical Hessian.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests batch-size learning-rate scaling and reports CIFAR-100 training outcomes, rather than systematically testing random initialization, label corruption, or the full set of model-size and stopping conditions in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size, optimizer, learning rate, batch normalization, and weight decay affect reported training outcomes or scaling behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Doubling the reference SGD learning-rate schedule initially accelerates training but later produces instability and divergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An initially productive learning rate can become unstable later in mini-batch cross-entropy training; this experiment does not establish its position relative to V5's initial stability threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: The study derives and validates linear batch-size scaling for SGD and square-root scaling for Adam, up to thresholds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The appropriate learning-rate scaling with batch size depends on the optimizer and curvature regime.

record.problems: Some training-error outcomes are shown only in figures, without exact values in the text. The text does not state initialization details for the near-100% training-accuracy comparison. The experiments focus on learning-rate scaling, not a systematic test of random initialization or label corruption.
record.rows_left_out: Training-error curves for other batch sizes and learning-rate schedules are figure-only and were not transcribed as separate rows; R3 captures the explicitly described no-training condition, and R1–R2 capture stated training accuracies.

untested.parts: Corrupted or random labels, CIFAR-10 training outcomes, model-size comparisons, and systematic early-stopping or regularization comparisons are untested. Random initialization details are unspecified. Adam training outcomes are presented in Figures 10 and 20–24, although omitted from the record's rows.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons are untested.
Depth-dependent degradation, matched shortcut comparisons, special tanh initializations, and Fixup are untested.
Initialization comparisons and their effects on learning speed or trainable depth are untested.

Recovery above a measured initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction during recovery, full-batch edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence from a measured below-threshold start are untested.
A controlled comparison isolating batch normalization's effect on accuracy gain or permissible learning rates is absent; the relevant VGG comparisons also change weight decay. Fixup is untested.

missing.what: A separate training-failure result: VGG-16 trained with initial learning rate 0.2 and zero weight decay remains at random performance after 100 epochs and does not recover after reducing the learning rate or increasing weight decay.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for any listed version. Other training curves are explicitly declared in rows_left_out and are therefore not listed as missing. The Figure 14 caption contradicts itself about weight decay; Section 10 specifies γ = 0.0005.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label training, CIFAR-10, Adam training error, smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes as a cause of substantial residual training error are not tested as stated.
